chunk_findings.detail: The old line filtered the resolved decisions to those the state actually holds (`if d.id in st.decisions`) before subscripting `st.decisions[rec.id]`; the new code drops that guard and does `d = st.decisions[did]` for every id returned by `AB.decision_order(applied, ...)`. `applied` comes from `GI.for_item(...).applied`, and the only filter applied to it is `a.record.kind == "decision"` — nothing checks that the id is a key of `st.decisions`. The removed `if d.id in st.decisions` is direct evidence that `for_item(...)` can resolve a decision record that is not present in `st.decisions` (e.g. a record present in the guidance store but not loaded/superseded in state). Given such an item, `applied` yields that decision, `decision_order` puts its id in `ranked`, and line 29 raises `KeyError`, crashing `ddflow brief --for-agent` — whereas before the item rendered fine with that decision simply excluded. chunk_findings.detail: `pinned = sum(1 for i in cfg.session.agent_brief_pin_decisions if i in st.decisions)` counts every occurrence in the configured list, but the head that `_decision_lines` actually emits is deduplicated — `AB.decision_order` builds it with `dict.fromkeys(pins)` and `_decision_lines` renders that deduped head one line per id. The slice is therefore sized by a count that can exceed the number of pin lines, so the knob's cap breaks again. Given `agent_brief_decisions = 2` and `agent_brief_pin_decisions = ["D-a", "D-a", "D-b"]` with all three ids present in `st.decisions`, `pinned` becomes 3, `shown = max(2, 3) = 3`, and `facts.decisions[:3]` quotes D-a, D-b plus the top-ranked non-pinned decision — one more decision than the knob permits, which is exactly the crowding-out the change exists to prevent. Counting unique pinned ids (or slicing by `len(head)`) would keep the slice consistent with the emitted lines.

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier review reported that the filter `if d.id in st.decisions` was dropped, so the code now does `d = st.decisions[did]` for every id yielded by `AB.decision_order(applied, ...)`, where `applied` comes from `GI.for_item(...).applied` and is only filtered on `a.record.kind == "decision"` — nothing guarantees the id is a key of `st.decisions`. That finding is still untriaged, and nothing visible in this change answers it: the new tests (`_decide` / `test_unknown_pinned_ids_do_not_widen_the_cap`) add every decision through `run_cli(..., "decision", "add", ...)`, which always populates `st.decisions`, so they never construct the failing input. Given a state in which an item carries an applied decision record whose id was never registered in `st.decisions` (e.g. an imported/pruned/orphaned decision id), `decision_order` returns that id and line 29 raises `KeyError` instead of the old code's silent skip — the brief crashes rather than omitting the unknown decision. None of the new assertions (glob ranking, pin ordering, cap widening) exercises or protects that path, so the defect stands.

chunk_findings.detail: This is the previously reported, still-untriaged finding [2], and the visible part of the new change does not answer it. The candidate set handed to `AB.decision_order` is built from `GI.for_item(...).applied` filtered only on `a.record.kind == "decision"`; nothing in the change shown constrains those ids to keys of the repo's own store, yet the render loop then indexes `st.decisions[did]`. Given input where the global index surfaces an applicable decision whose id is not a key of `st.decisions` (an inherited/global decision, or an entry indexed from a store other than this repo's decision file) — say the brief is run as `ddflow brief --for-agent a T1 --phase P1` while the item's applied decisions include such an id — the lookup raises `KeyError` and the command dies with a traceback instead of emitting the brief. The newly added `test_unknown_pinned_ids_do_not_widen_the_cap` is not a probe for this: it only passes unknown ids through `session.agent_brief_pin_decisions` (the pin path), while every decision it creates with `_decide` exists in `st.decisions`, so the applied/unpinned path that does the unguarded lookup is never exercised. The finding therefore still holds.

chunk_findings.detail: `TS.run_command` receives the whole-suite command as its first argument and falls back to it when the file list is empty. When a change selects no tests (`sel.tests == []`, e.g. a docs-only or config-only change), `files` is empty, so `data["command"]` becomes the full 13k-test command. The new `if not show_full:` block clears `full_suite` and `advice`, but not `command`, so `ddflow tests` (without `--full`) still prints the whole-suite command as the command to run, with no "MERGE QUEUE / PHASE END ONLY" label and with the parallel/host-lock advice suppressed. Given a repo with a configured `unit_tests` gate and a change that touches no test-mapped files, an agent following the printed command again runs the entire suite — the exact fleet-dx-e failure this change is meant to prevent. The `--full` gate needs to cover this fallback too (e.g. emit an empty/"no tests selected" command when `files` is empty).

chunk_findings.detail:
The first sort component `a.reason != GLOBS or broad` collapses two separate tiers into one bucket: decisions that *do* overlap the item's globs but only through a broad `**`, and decisions that do not overlap the item's globs at all. The function's own docstring says the order is "those whose own globs overlap the item's (a broad `**` last of them) ... then the rest by enforcement and id" — i.e. a broad-glob match is still ahead of the non-overlapping rest — but the code gives both the same first key value and then lets `operator`/enforcement/priority/id decide, so a non-overlapping decision can be emitted before a broad-glob decision and vice versa.

Concrete failure: item globs `["src/**"]`, decision A = `{reason: GLOBS, scope.globs: ["**"], origin: agent, enforcement: "advisory", id: "D-a"}`, decision B = `{reason: TAG, origin: operator, enforcement: "block", id: "D-z"}`. Then `key(A) = (True, True, 2, 0, "D-a")` and `key(B) = (True, False, 0, 0, "D-z")`, so B is ranked first even though only A is a glob match for these files; with the operands swapped (A operator, B agent) the code ranks A first, i.e. broad-glob decisions are interleaved with the "rest" rather than being ordered last as documented. Either way, a broad `**` decision gets the wrong position relative to non-overlapping decisions (the exact "irrelevant decisions crowd out the relevant ones" behaviour the change is meant to remove). A three-valued first component (`0` = glob match, non-broad; `1` = glob match, broad; `2` = no glob overlap) is what the docstring describes; the current boolean merges levels 1 and 2.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/agent_brief.py: `decision_order` (the first element of `key`)

chunk_findings.detail: The test never sets up an item with globs, and the four decisions' globs are `""`, `"**"`, `"src/**"`, `"src/widget.py"` — i.e. the asserted order (`D-op-match` < `D-agent-match` < `D-broad` < `D-unscoped`) is exactly what a pure "glob specificity, then no-glob-last" sort produces, with no matching against any item's files involved (`src/widget.py` is never created, yet it is expected first). Because of this the test cannot detect the two behaviors it is named for: (a) it never demonstrates that a decision whose glob *matches the item's globs* outranks one that merely has a *more specific* glob; and (b) it never demonstrates operator-over-agent precedence — drop operator precedence entirely and the same assertion still passes, since `D-broad` (operator, `"**"`) is in fact asserted *below* `D-agent-match` (agent, `"src/**"`). The only test for the change's stated "operator decisions rank above agent ones" / "rank by glob match against the item's globs" guarantees is therefore vacuous, and a regression that ranked by raw glob specificity over actual match (the original crowding-out problem) would go green.

chunk_findings.detail: The intent requires the surplus decisions to be surfaced as "N more: ddflow decision applicable <id>". Here two decisions exist with cap 1, so exactly one decision is dropped into that remainder, but the test only asserts `ids[0] == "D-standing"` and `"D-op-match" not in ids` — it never asserts the remainder line, its count, or its id. An implementation that silently drops over-cap decisions (printing no "N more" hint at all, or the wrong count/id) passes this test, so the feature's stated output contract is unguarded.

chunk_findings.detail:
The change does not separate "overlaps the item's globs only through a broad `**`" from "does not overlap the item's globs at all": both still evaluate to the same first-key boolean (`a.reason != GLOBS or broad`), so inside that bucket ordering falls through to enforcement and then id. Concrete failing input: an item whose globs are `src/**`, plus two operator decisions — `D-aaa-other` with globs `aaa/**` (no overlap with the item) and `D-broad` with globs `**` (overlaps). Because the glob-overlap tier is collapsed, `"D-aaa-other" < "D-broad"` by id, so the non-overlapping decision is emitted *ahead* of the broad-glob decision, contradicting the function's own docstring ("those whose own globs overlap the item's (a broad `**` last of them) … then the rest by enforcement and id"), which still places any overlapping decision ahead of the non-overlapping rest.

The new test does not answer this, so the earlier finding still holds: `test_decisions_rank_glob_matches_before_unscoped_and_operator_before_agent` never builds an item with globs (it calls `brief(proj)` with no target and no item is created, `src/widget.py` is only a string literal), and its sole broad-vs-unscoped pair (`D-broad` globs `**`, `D-unscoped` no globs) are both `by="operator"`, so the collapsed key still produces the asserted order via the `"D-broad" < "D-unscoped"` id tie-break. A correct 3-tier implementation and the collapsed 2-tier implementation both pass this test, so nothing in the diff demonstrates the collapse was fixed.
